segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Thirty-Eight. Triangles on equal bases and in the same parallels are equal in area. Let triangles A B C and D E F stand on equal bases B C and E F and lie between the same parallel lines B F and A D. We prove that triangle A B C is equal in area to triangle D E F.

segments.text: Then each of the figures G B C A and D E F H is a parallelogram on equal bases B C and E F and between the same parallels B F and G H. By Proposition Thirty-Six, parallelogram G B C A is equal in area to parallelogram D E F H. By Proposition Thirty-Four, the diagonal A B bisects parallelogram G B C A, so triangle A B C is half of parallelogram G B C A. Likewise, the diagonal D F bisects parallelogram D E F H, so triangle D E F is half of parallelogram D E F H. Since the halves of equal things are equal to one another, triangle A B C is equal in area to triangle D E F, as was required to prove.
